tests.name: datetime
tests.description: Date/time arithmetic and the date/time functions: Date, DateTime and Time plus and minus a calendar duration (singular, plural or the quoted keyword) or the UCUM units 's' and 'ms', per component (years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds) with month-end and leap-year handling, the year out of the Date range, the decimal portion ignored above seconds, partial precision (the quantity converted to the value's highest precision and truncated), timezone offsets carried through, Time wrapping around midnight (3.0.0), negative quantities through unary minus (3.0.0), the UCUM 'a' and 'mo' refused, date components refused on a Time and time components on a Date, other right operands refused, empty and multi-item operands, and FHIR dates and Age quantities in arithmetic; now(), today() and timeOfDay() by their type and determinism only; and 3.0.0's lowBoundary()/highBoundary() with a precision and precision() on Date, DateTime and Time, the component functions yearOf to timeOf, and duration() and difference(). Date plus time units is an error as 3.0.0 states; 2.0.0 lists the units a Date takes without a consequence, so 3.0.0 defines what 2.0.0 does not. Left out because the text does not settle them: the UCUM units 'wk', 'd', 'h' and 'min' on a Date or DateTime (3.0.0 accepts them; 2.0.0 contradicts itself, saying both that a definite-quantity duration above seconds signals an error and that a DateTime or Time takes an equivalent unit, which its table makes 'wk', 'd', 'h' and 'min'), fractional weeks, fractional days or hours added to a value of second or millisecond precision, fractional seconds on a value coarser than milliseconds, fractional milliseconds, results out of range other than by adding years to a Date (in particular a DateTime whose year leaves 0001 to 9999: both texts say implementations can provide support for larger ranges for DateTime, and say no such thing for Date), the minimum precision of now(), today() compared with now(), lowBoundary()/highBoundary() without a precision on Date, DateTime and Time, with a precision the type does not have or below the value's, or on an unzoned DateTime under R5's page, precision() of a value with a timezone offset or with other than three fractional digits, timeOf() of a DateTime without seconds, and duration()/difference() with a precision the type does not allow, mixed types, a multi-item or empty argument, or month ends. Comparison and equality of temporals (equality-comparison.xml), toDate/toDateTime/toTime and literal syntax (a later conversions area), and lowBoundary()/highBoundary() on decimals and on an empty input (fhir-functions.xml) are not repeated.

group.name: REQ-DATETIME-013
group.description: Time is cyclic: adding or subtracting past midnight wraps around the day (3.0.0, STU; 2.0.0 does not say)
group.source: As `Time` is cyclic, using arithmetic operations `+` or `-` on `Time` types can result in overflowing the time value, which will wrap around the beginning of the day.
So adding 1 hour to `@T23:30:00` will wrap around to `@T00:30:00`, which is consistent with the behaviour of `DateTime` values.
@T23:30:00 + 1 hour // @T00:30:00 ; overflow midnight
@T01:00:00 + 48 hour // @T01:00:00 ; cycles through twice, but resulting time is the same

group.source: For partial date/time values where the time-valued quantity is more precise than the partial date/time, the operation is performed by converting the time-valued quantity to the highest precision in the partial (removing any decimal value off) and then adding to the date/time value.

The first example above returns @2015, because 23 months only constitutes one year. The second example returns 2017 because even though 2016 is a leap-year, the time-valued quantity (`365 days`) is converted to `1 year`, a standard calendar year of 365 days.

For partial date/time values where the time-valued quantity is more precise than the partial date/time, the operation is performed by converting the time-valued quantity to the highest precision in the partial (truncating any decimal fraction) and then adding to the date/time value.

E.g. the lowBoundary of 1.0 is 0.95000000000 , and the lowBoundary of 2010-10-10 is 2010-10-10T00:00:00.000+14:00 .
E.g. the highBoundary of 1.0 is 1.05000000000 , and the highBoundary of 2010-10-10 is 2010-10-10T23:59:59.999-12:00 .

group.name: REQ-DATETIME-059
group.description: duration() counts the whole calendar periods between the input and the value, as 3.0.0's examples (3.0.0 alone, STU)

source.section: duration(value: Date | DateTime | Time, precision: String): Integer

group.source: Returns the number of whole calendar periods at the specified `precision` between the given input value and the `value` argument. If the input value is after the `value` argument, the result is negative. The result of this operation is always an integer; any fractional periods are dropped.

source.section: duration(value: Date | DateTime | Time, precision: String): Integer

group.source: @2025-01-02.duration(@2025-01-07, 'week') // 0 ; hasn't passed 7 days duration

source.section: duration(value: Date | DateTime | Time, precision: String): Integer

group.source: @2025-01-01.duration(@2025-09-01, 'year') // 0 ; baby is 9 months old

source.section: duration(value: Date | DateTime | Time, precision: String): Integer

group.source: @2024-12-01.duration(@2025-09-01, 'year') // 0 ; baby is 10 months old
